name: The Bildeiche at Höhenhof

location.address: Meadow about 600 m south-west of the hamlet Höhenhof, beside the road to Obertraubling, DBU Naturerbe Frauenholz, 93083 Obertraubling

official_register.name: Bavarian LfU Naturdenkmal register ND-02810 (Landkreis Regensburg ND list no. 47)

access: Stands in a meadow on the DBU Naturerbe Frauenholz (former military training area, managed by Bundesforstbetrieb Hohenfels); baumkunde.de lists access as publicly accessible and the road to Obertraubling passes the tree. The trunk opening with the Madonna figure is behind a grille.
transport: About 8 km south of Regensburg centre near Obertraubling/Oberhinkofen. Bus connection and travel time NOT verified (no timetable found); day-trip boundary unconfirmed.
story:
A Madonna stands inside this oak. Long ago a thick limb broke away about a metre above the ground, the wound left a hollow in the trunk, and a figure of the Mother of God was set into it. That is the name: a Bildeiche is an oak with a picture in it. A grille now closes the opening, and there is no other in the trunk.

It is 7.20 metres round, measured in September 2021 by Rainer Lippert, who records Germany's monumental oaks, and 19 metres tall, with a crown built from several heavy limbs going their own way. Lippert puts it at roughly 350 years. That is his estimate, not a ring count, so read it as somewhere between 300 and 400. The tree register baumkunde.de carries the same figures, partly from the same observer, which makes it less of a second opinion than it looks.

Bavaria made it a natural monument on 15 January 1938. The ground around it was military land from 1861 to 2011, a training area from 1958, and Lippert writes that the oak is missing from the literature: a friend of his came across it by chance. Today the meadow belongs to the 494 hectare DBU Naturerbe Frauenholz, the road to Obertraubling runs past, and the tree was last reported in good health in August 2024.

It stands about 8 km south of Regensburg, near Obertraubling. We have not checked the buses, so look up the route before you set out.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the grilled hollow about a metre up the trunk, with a Madonna figure inside. It stands on its own in a meadow beside the road to Obertraubling, about 600 m south-west of Höhenhof.

name: The Wutzlhofen Oak

official_register.name: Stadt Regensburg, Naturdenkmal Nr. 51 (Verordnung vom 4 Feb 1994)

access: Free, always open: stands on the small village green with a fountain and benches in the middle of Wutzlhofen, beside the public road.
transport: Regensburg city bus to Wutzlhofen; line and stop not verified, so unchecked. About 4 km north-east of the old town.
story:
Regensburg protects this oak for being the middle of a village. The ordinance that made it natural monument number 51 on 4 February 1994 says so in as many words: the oak is to be kept as the centre of Wutzlhofen, for its outstanding beauty and its age.

The same ordinance put that age at about 180 to 200 years in 1994. Carried forward, that makes it somewhere past two centuries now, roughly 210 to 230, though it is the city's own round figure and not a ring count. Either way the oak was already more than a hundred years old in 1924, when Wutzlhofen became part of Regensburg.

The place is far older than the tree. Wutzlhofen first appears in 1224 as Wuzenhoven, a property of the Regensburg cathedral chapter. The oak's protection reaches 11 metres out from the middle of its trunk, and around it is a small green with a fountain, five benches and two seesaw animals, opposite house number 42, about 4 km north-east of the old town.

It is no champion. It is a village tree doing the job the village gave it. The city still listed it in 2020, and we have found no dated photograph since. Nobody has published its girth, its height or which oak it is. If you know, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the oak on Wutzlhofen's small village green, with a fountain and benches close by. It stands beside the road, opposite house number 42.

Register: city ordinance (AMBl. 8, 21 Feb 1994, amended 12 Dec 2001) protects the oak on plot Flur-Nr. 808/27, Gemarkung Sallern, with a protected radius of 11 m round the trunk centre. Stated purpose: keep the oak as the centre ('Mittelpunkt') of the district of Wutzlhofen, for its outstanding beauty and age 'ca. 180 bis 200 Jahre' AT 1994 (so roughly 210 to 230 now; widened to 200 to 250, derived from the ordinance). No girth or height published. Species given only as Eiche; genus oak, ask the reader which species. Setting: komoot highlight describes the oak as the 'centre' of the village, in a small green area with a fountain, five benches and two seesaw animals, like a small park. Wutzlhofen first documented 1224 as 'Wuzenhoven', property of the Regensburg cathedral chapter; part of Regensburg only since 1924. Alive: lifecheck.py returned NONE (no recent dated observation found), ordinance and 2020s city ND list (Stand 2020) still carry it, komoot lists it as a visitable highlight; flagged for thin recent confirmation. No Commons photo found by category name (Category:Wutzlhofener Eiche does not exist); photo not hunted per brief. Tree is a village-green oak of modest size, worth the visit mainly as a living village centre, not a champion.

name: The Unterisling Oaks

location.address: Stadlerstrasse (east of no. 11), Papstwiese / Islinger Feld, 93053 Regensburg

official_register.name: Stadt Regensburg, Naturdenkmal Nr. 50 (Verordnung vom 26 May 1993)

access: Free. The four oaks stand beside a public footway (OSM way 28290618: highway=footway, access=yes, foot=yes) at the edge of the Islinger Feld meadow (OSM landuse=meadow). Trees are on a field plot; view from the path.
transport: South-east of the old town in Unterisling, about 5 km from the centre; bus line and stop not verified, so unchecked.
story:
Regensburg protects these four oaks as one monument, and the field around them with them. City ordinance number 50, signed on 26 May 1993, covers the four trees and about 1,400 square metres of the plot they stand on, at the edge of the Islinger Feld meadow in Unterisling. The city's list calls the spot the Papstwiese, the Pope's meadow.

The ordinance gives three reasons: their outstanding beauty, their age, and the way they shape the look of the village. It does not say what that age is, and nothing else we have found does either. There is no girth, no height and no planting date for any of the four, which makes them the least documented trees on this page and a clean example of Regensburg protecting a tree without measuring it.

They were standing on 19 April 2024, when a naturalist photographed them and logged them as pedunculate oaks. Nobody has confirmed that guess, so here they are simply oaks.

A public footpath runs past them, and the trees themselves stand on a field plot, so these are oaks to see from the path rather than to walk under. The four trunks are spread over about 45 metres, close enough to take in from one place. If you know which oak they are, or how old, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as four oaks standing together, spread over about 45 metres at the edge of the Islinger Feld meadow. They stand beside the public footpath east of Stadlerstrasse 11.
verify_notes: Register: city ordinance Naturdenkmal Nr. 50 of 26 May 1993 protects four oaks ('vier Eichen') on Flur-Nr. 566, Gemarkung Oberisling, plus about 1,400 sq m of surroundings. Stated purpose: outstanding beauty, age and village-scene character ('Schoenheit und Alters sowie des ortsbildpraegenden Charakters'). No ages, girths or heights published anywhere found. Pin: four OSM natural=tree nodes named 'Die Unterislinger Eichen' with monument=yes (ids 1579655283, 3423607721, 3423607722, 3423607723), spread over roughly 45 m (48.98317,12.12071 to 48.98352,12.12102); pin given is the group centre. A registered group of four within 50 m with one place to stand is a single collectible ensemble. Alive: iNaturalist observation 208260893 (19 Apr 2024, by Hermann Josef Eckl, located 48.98328,12.12078 at the oaks); observer guessed Stieleiche (Quercus robur), unconfirmed community id, so species stays genus level; photo is CC BY-NC so NOT usable. lifecheck.py: RECENT 2024-04-19. The register list calls the spot 'Papstwiese' (the field of the 12 Sept 2006 papal Mass per a search snippet, not fetched, so unverified); no source links the oaks to that event, so do not bridge. No Commons category found for the group. Flag: no age or girth, so what makes them remarkable is only the register's own 'beauty and age' wording; ask the reader for species and age.
